data.long_meaning: In the Battle of Uhud, Muhaisin ibn Nawfal Al-Ashja'i was a brave warrior who fought against the enemy despite being injured. He was supported by his comrades, leading to the name Muhaisan which means 'the one who is supported'. The name Muhaisan carries the meaning “The One Who Is Supported” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muhaisan usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who is supported and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The site of the battle is believed to be near the modern-day town of Mafraq. Muhaisan ibn Abi Sasanah, an Arab Christian warlord, was allied with the Byzantines and led their forces in the battle. He was eventually captured and executed by the Muslims.

historical_references.context: Muhaisan ibn Abi Sasanah, after his capture in the Battle of Mu'tah, was presented before Muhammad in Medina. He was offered the option of converting to Islam or facing execution. Muhaisan, who was a Christian, chose to remain steadfast in his faith and was subsequently executed. This event is considered significant in Islamic history as an example of the early Muslim community's commitment to religious freedom and tolerance, as well as their willingness to engage in military campaigns against non-Muslim powers.
